title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response & Compliance Evidence Control Framework
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This document consolidates the Security & Compliance control expectations for Redwood Inference across: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC, security-focused incident response procedures, compliance evidence collection workflows, and risk & exceptions handling. It is intended for engineering, product, security, and compliance stakeholders and supports audits (SOC2, ISO27001, and customer due diligence).

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services (API gateway, inference runtime, control plane, console), Dedicated and Private deployment packaging, and supporting infra (CI/CD, logging, monitoring).
- Excludes third-party vendor controls which are documented in vendor-specific contracts and the Vendor Security Registry.

Owner & Contacts:
- Primary owner: Security (Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owners: Eng Infra (Marcus Rivera), Eng SRE (Lily Zhang)
- Pager / Incident contact: #security-pager in PagerDuty; escalation list maintained in Oncall directory.

1) RBAC and Authentication

Principles:
- Least privilege by default. Roles are narrowly scoped and assigned to groups (not individual users) wherever possible.
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) required for all interactive access.
- Centralized identity provider (IdP) with SCIM provisioning for automated group management.

Authentication stack (standard deployments):
- IdP: Okta (primary) with fallback to GSuite SSO for specific business units.
- Service identity: short-lived workload credentials issued by auth-service using OIDC / AWS STS (or GCP Workload Identity for GCP-hosted infra).
- Secrets & keys: HashiCorp Vault for service-level secrets; KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) for envelope encryption of customer keys.

RBAC model and role definitions (summary):
- viewer: read-only access to dashboards and documentation.
- developer: ability to create and manage non-production resources (dev/test).
- operator: deploy/runbook access, ability to manage production config under approval.
- oncall: escalations and incident controls, constrained to runbook actions.
- admin: full access; limited to a small group (SRE leads + Security) and audited quarterly.

Key controls and operational rules:
- All production role assignments require an approved JIT (just-in-time) expiring role or ticket in the access request system.
- Quarterly access reviews: ownership list stored in /security/access-reviews; evidence exported as CSV to evidence-bucket for audits.
- Privileged sessions (admin) are recorded and routed to Splunk for retention and review.

2) Audit Logging

Objectives:
- Ensure immutable, tamper-evident logging of authentication events, privileged actions, configuration changes, and inference-control-plane API calls.
- Provide timely delivery to SIEM for detection and investigation.

Logging architecture:
- Agents: fluentd deployed as a DaemonSet (k8s) and as sidecars for legacy services.
- Aggregation: logs are forwarded to an audit-log-collector cluster then delivered to S3 (us-east-1) / GCS (europe-west1) for long term storage and to Splunk (real-time index) for analysis.
- Integrity: logs are hashed (SHA256) and signed with a rotation-aware audit key. Hash manifests are stored in the evidence-bucket and accessible to auditors.

SLOs & thresholds:
- Audit log delivery: 99.9% of events delivered to Splunk within 5 minutes.
- Alerting on missing heartbeats: Pager if no audit-log-collector heartbeat for > 5 minutes.

Retention & access:
- Default service logs retention: 90 days in Splunk hot tier, 1 year in warm tier, and archived to object storage for 7 years for controls subject to financial/regulatory requirements.
- Access to raw audit archives requires approval from Security and Legal and is performed via an evidence request process.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Policy summary:
- Customer data (inputs, outputs, embeddings, keys) residency is honored per contract and region setting. Default hosted data residency: US and EU regions depending on customer selection.
- Retention baselines: default 90 days for ephemeral inference traces, 365 days for customer-configured logs, and up to 7 years for regulated accounts (finance/healthcare) per contract.

Implementation details:
- Region isolation: storage buckets and KMS keys are region-scoped. When a customer selects EU residency, we provision GCP/eu buckets and KMS in europe-west1 and enforce routing via smart routing policies.
- Deletion procedures: documented deletion job (delete-customer-data) that performs a staged deletion (mark -> purge after retention period) and writes an audit record.

Verification & evidence:
- Residency proof: periodic exports of bucket metadata and KMS key ARNs sampled monthly and stored in evidence-bucket.
- Retention proofs: retention policies are configured as lifecycle rules on buckets; snapshots of these rules are taken monthly.

4) Secure SDLC

Goals:
- Embed security checks into CI/CD: static analysis, dependency scanning, secret scanning, and SCA for all builds.
- Gate production deployments on passing security gates and required approvals.

Pipeline controls:
- CI (buildkite): every PR triggers tests + unit + integration + security checks. Security checks include: Trivy for container images, Snyk for dependency scanning, and git-secrets for secret detection.
- IaC: Terraform modules must pass policy-as-code checks (Sentinel / Open Policy Agent) before apply.
- Review & approval: production changes require two approvers, one of which must be from Security or SRE for infra changes.

Developer guidance:
- Secrets must never be checked into git. Use Vault + dynamic secrets and reference via buildkite-vault-plugin.
- Security PR checklist (required): threat model updated, risk accepted or mitigated, performance impact reviewed, rollout plan included.

5) Incident Response (Security) Procedures

Goals:
- Contain and mitigate security incidents quickly, preserve evidence, and minimize customer impact while meeting notification obligations.

Triage & classification:
- Incident severity levels: Sev1 (customer-facing data breach), Sev2 (service compromise with limited exposure), Sev3 (internal security event).
- Initial triage: security oncall to acknowledge within 15 minutes and classify.

Preservation of evidence:
- For any incident that may touch customer data or admin privileges, snapshot audit logs, compute instance metadata, and relevant S3/GCS objects immediately. Use incident-runbook/collect-evidence.sh to standardize artifacts.
- Mark evidence buckets as inadvertent-access-readonly and preserve for 90 days by default for investigation.

Coordination & communication:
- Runbooks: the security runbook library (confluence: /security/runbooks) contains step-by-step containment and eradication playbooks.
- Customer notification: Legal + CSM decide on notification timelines; PII breaches follow contractual/regulated timelines (e.g., 72 hours where applicable under GDPR).

Post-incident:
- Postmortem template: security postmortems must include timeline, root cause, remediation, compensating controls, and evidence links. All security postmortems undergo an independent review within 7 days.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Evidence lifecycle summary:
- Sources of truth: access control exports, audit log manifests, retention policy snapshots, code scanning results, and deployment approvals.
- Storage: evidence-bucket (encrypted with customer- and company-level KMS keys) with ACLs scoped to compliance team.

Typical evidence collection flows:
1. Scheduled exports: monthly exports of access lists, role assignments, and policy snapshots stored under /evidence/monthly/YYYY-MM.
2. Audit-triggered exports: for an audit request we run the evidence-assemble job which produces a ZIP with signed manifests and a chain-of-custody CSV.
3. Incident-driven evidence: evidence preserved during incidents is cataloged and linked to ticket IDs (e.g., PD-INC-1234).

Evidence format expectations:
- CSV/JSON manifest files with SHA256 hashes for each artifact.
- Human-readable executive summary (PDF) explaining controls and any exceptions.

Compliance requests & SLAs:
- Standard evidence request SLA: 5 business days for routine requests, 48 hours for high-priority audit or regulatory requests.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Risk acceptance process:
- Any deviation from the standard control baseline must be documented via an exception request in the Risk Registry. The request must include: owner, timeframe, compensating controls, and risk rating.
- Short-lived exceptions (<= 30 days) require Security approver; long-lived exceptions (> 30 days) require Security + CISO + Product approval.

Monitoring exceptions:
- Exceptions are tracked as tickets and reviewed monthly in the Risk Review board. Evidence of mitigations must be provided before extension.

Common exception examples and mitigations:
- Exception: temporary elevated admin access for third-party contractor. Mitigations: JIT access, session recording enabled, 24/7 monitoring on the account, and automated expiry.
- Exception: cross-region data transfer during migration. Mitigations: encrypted in transit with TLS1.3, dual-control approvals, and targeted log capture for the migration window.

Appendix: Config snippets and commands

1) Example access review export (CLI):
$ ./scripts/export-access.sh --quarter Q4-2027 --out evidence/access-Q4-2027.csv

2) Audit log integrity check (pseudo):
$ audit-checker --bucket s3://audit-archive-prod --manifest manifests/2027-12-01.sha256

3) Evidence assemble (example invocation):
$ ./tools/evidence-assemble --request-id AR-2027-334 --output /tmp/AR-2027-334.zip

Ownership & Cadence (summary)
- Security: control owner and quarterly review of RBAC, audit integrity, and retention rules.
- Eng Infra: monthly verification of KMS and bucket configs.
- Compliance: monthly evidence-sanity checks and annual audit preparation.
